title: Why Is the Sky Blue?

shots.note: Earth from space — atmosphere, not paint
Blue scatter between sun and Earth

narration: Nobody climbed up there with a giant paintbrush.
Sunlight looks white, but it is many colors mixed together.
Red, orange, yellow, green, blue — all riding in the same beam.
Let me show you that in 3D.
The air around us is full of tiny bits you cannot see.
Those bits scatter the blue light more than the other colors.
So blue fills the sky we see.
Watch this next bit closely. This is why it happens.
At sunset, the light travels farther through the air.
The blue gets scattered away. Warmer colors win the show.
Then you can look up and know the trick.
Remember: the sky isn’t painted. Air and sunlight make the blue.
And that is the whole idea, in one short 3D film.
description:
Why is the sky blue? A kid-safe cinematic Blender 3D short (ages 6–10).
